scope: Official release history, release chronology, API reference, and version-pinned SQLite 3.54.1 source

claims.claim: SQLite 3.52.0 was withdrawn because of backwards-compatibility concerns involving expression indexes and floating-point values derived from text or JSONB
SQLite 3.53.0 was released on 2026-04-09, fixed the WAL-reset corruption bug, and included enhancements for stale expression indexes
SQLite 3.53.0 introduced QRF and the documented ALTER TABLE, REINDEX EXPRESSIONS, TEMP trigger, VACUUM INTO and JSON array insertion changes
Since 3.53.0, SQLite attempts to repair stale expression index entries in some UPDATE or DELETE cases, while integrity_check can still report imprecise floating-point values
REINDEX EXPRESSIONS rebuilds expression indexes and leaves ordinary indexes unchanged
claims.locator: §5 How To Avoid And/Or Fix Stale Expression Indexes

claims.claim: SQLite 3.53.0 changed default floating-point to text rounding from 15 to 17 significant digits and exposes SQLITE_DBCONFIG_FP_DIGITS
claims.notes: This does not change IEEE-754 binary64 storage precision.

claims.claim: SQLite 3.54.0 introduced CLI, query planner, C API, platform and performance changes documented in the release history
sqlite3_result_str accepts sqlite3_context*, sqlite3_str*, and an ownership flag
claims.notes: It does not accept an ordinary char* and length.

claims.claim: The Windows non-recursive SQLite mutex implementation uses AcquireSRWLockExclusive while recursive mutexes use CRITICAL_SECTION
claims.notes: Do not describe this as shared-reader locking.

claims.claim: The Unix VFS uses O_TMPFILE only when built on Linux with O_TMPFILE support
SQLite 3.54.1 fixes a possible heap-buffer overflow on some 32-bit builds; 64-bit builds are not affected by this specific issue
The release history reports about 4% speedtest1 CPU-cycle improvement under Valgrind on Linux x64, not a workload-independent latency guarantee
claims.notes: The same entry reports about 7.5% compared with 3.51.0.

claims.claim: SQLite chronology lists 3.53.6 on 2026-11-13 and 3.54.1 on 2026-10-16 as distinct maintenance lines
claims.notes: A later date on an older maintenance branch does not replace a higher-version branch.

claims.claim: Claims of a new generic star-join algorithm or a broad sorted-merge rewrite are not included as 3.53.0 features without a verified release note or check-in
claims.notes: Absence from the release summary is not a universal proof that no internal change exists; the chapter intentionally makes no such claim.
